hints: Notice you have the same mass of each carbonate, so think in moles rather than grams to compare how much $\text{CO}_2$ can form.
Each carbonate ion gives one $\text{CO}_2$ molecule, so work out which 1.0 g sample contains the most moles by finding the smallest $M_r$.
Divide 1.0 g by each $M_r$ to compare moles of carbonate, and the largest mole value will give the largest amount of $\text{CO}_2$.
walkthrough:
**Write the reaction idea**

All carbonates react with excess acid to release one mole of $\text{CO}_2$ per mole of carbonate. Acid is in excess, so the carbonate is limiting.

Chemical equation idea:
$$\text{CO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Use moles = mass / Mr**

For the same mass, the compound with the smallest $M_r$ gives the most moles, and therefore the most $\text{CO}_2$. Let's compare $M_r$ values.

Calculation rule:
$$n(\text{CO}_2) = n(\text{carbonate}) = \frac{1.0}{M_r}$$

**Compare the four Mr values**

$\text{CaCO}_3 \approx 100$, $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3 \approx 73.9$, $\text{MgCO}_3 \approx 84.3$, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \approx 106$. The smallest is $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$, so 1.0 g of it contains about 0.0135 mol, more than any other, and releases the largest amount of $\text{CO}_2$.

options.A: 1.0 g $\text{CaCO}_3$ gives about $1.0/100.1 = 0.0100$ mol of $\text{CO}_2$. This is less than the lightest carbonate, so it is not the largest.
options.B: 1.0 g $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$ has $M_r \approx 73.9$, the smallest of the four. Moles $= 1.0/73.9 \approx 0.0135$ mol, giving the most $\text{CO}_2$ because each mole of carbonate gives one mole of $\text{CO}_2$.
options.C: 1.0 g $\text{MgCO}_3$ gives about $1.0/84.3 = 0.0119$ mol of $\text{CO}_2$. This is second largest, but still less than $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$ because Mg is heavier than 2 Li.
options.D: 1.0 g $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ has the largest $M_r \approx 106$, so it gives only about $1.0/106 = 0.0094$ mol of $\text{CO}_2$, the smallest amount. A common trap is to think sodium compounds give more.
